notes: Cohort CONFIRMED. 'A longitudinal retrospective observational study was conducted to compare the costs and effects of EIP services with other community mental health teams (CMHTs) over a 3-year period (April 2010-March 2013) in the Oxford Academic Health Science Network (AHSN) region' (Methods, p. 2), covering 3.3 million people in Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Milton Keynes, Oxfordshire and Bedfordshire. Contributes two results, both blocked by an unresolved denominator conflict and both without any recoverable count.

Cohort CONFIRMED as the DETECT early intervention for psychosis service in Dublin: the author affiliations are 'Detect, St John of Gods, Dublin, Ireland', 'all cases of suspected FEP presenting to secondary mental health services in a geographical area were referred to the EIPS' and the admission process is that described by Renwick et al. (2015) (Methods, Recruitment, p. 116). The prospective follow-up study reported here is distinct from the matched historical-control study of the same programme published as Turner, O'Callaghan and Clarke (2016), which is not held; if that report is ever staged it shares this cohort_id and the historical controls are a separate sample.

Cohort CONFIRMED. 'The source population for this study was patients hospitalized at Peking University Institute of Mental Health in 2006 ... Patient records numbered 14,001 to 15,000 were consecutively assessed' (Methods, Inclusion criteria, p. 2 of 9). Single centre, single admission year, no linkage to any other staged report.

Cohort CONFIRMED as the JiSEF fidelity and service-process study: 'Through the scale development research for the JiSEF, we identified 25 agencies that at least partially provided supported employment programs for people with mental illness. Of these, 13 programs participated in the study' (Methods, Overall Design, p. 474). Participants may overlap with the Japanese pilot process study (Yamaguchi et al. 2017, Jpn J Psychiatr Rehabil) and possibly with the cognitive-remediation-plus-supported-employment RCT (Yamaguchi et al. 2017, Psychol Med); neither is held or staged, so no overlaps_with row can be written against a cohort that does not exist in this schema.

Cohort CONFIRMED. 'Between 2013 and 2015, 162 participants were recruited from Wuxi Mental Health Center' and randomised three ways; registered as NCT03273530 (Method, Participants, p. 7106165020p2; Acknowledgment, p. 7106165020p6). Two earlier pilot studies of the same programme at the same centre are cited (Li et al. 2013; Lu et al. 2015) and are not held; participant overlap with them is not stated.
